PROCEDURE NAME:  Upper extremity venograms.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with multiple HD thrombosis and non- maturing
AV fistula.  Both upper extremity venograms were requested for evaluation of
SVC stenosis.

RADIOLOGISTS:  This procedure was performed by Dr. ___ Dr. ___,
the attending radiologist, who was present and supervising throughout the
entire procedure.

PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS:  After explaining the risks and benefits of the
procedure, informed consent was obtained from the patient.  The patient was
placed supine on the angiographic table.  Both upper extremity venograms were
performed with contrast injection through the IV line of both lower arms.
Venogram demonstrated patent basilic vein, axillary vein, subclavian vein, and
both brachial veins and SVC.  However, collateral veins were noted about the
proximal  right subclavian vein and re-evaluation was needed.  During the
tunneled hemodialysis catheter placement, using a 9 ___ ___ sheath
and 5 ___ Kumpe catheter/0.035 ___ glidewire combination, access was
gained into the right subclavian vein and a venogram was performed
demonstrating a widely patent right subclavian vein, right brachiocephalic
vein and SVC, even though some collaterals were still noted. The patient
tolerated the procedure well and there were no immediate complication.

IMPRESSION:  Wideliy patent central veins including the subclavain veins and
brachiocephalic veins bilaterally. Small collateral veins were noted at the
level of the proximal right subclavain vein.

PROCEDURE NAME:  Exchange with a tunneled hemodialysis catheter.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with end-stage renal disease and non-maturing
right upper extremity AV fistula.  Exchange of left temporary HD catheter with
a tunneled hemodialysis catheter was requested.

RADIOLOGISTS:  This procedure was performed by Dr. ___ Dr. ___,
the attending radiologist, who was present and supervising throughout the
entire procedure.

PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS:  After explaining the risks and benefits of the
procedure, informed written informed consent was obtained from the patient.
The patient was placed supine on the angiographic table and the patient's left
neck and chest were prepped and draped in standard sterile fashion.  A
preprocedure timeout was performed.

After injection of 1% lidocaine at the left upper chest and exit site of
indwelling temporary HD catheter, an incision was made at the exit site of the
tunneled hemodialysis catheter.  A 15.5 ___ tunneled hemodialysis catheter
with 23 cm tip-to-cuff length was placed through the subcutaneous tunnel into
the neck incision site.  An Amplatz guidewire was advanced through the
indwelling temporary HD catheter into the IVC under fluoroscopic guidance and
indwelling temporary HD catheter was removed.
A ___ ___ tip sheath was advanced over the wire into the SVC and using a ___
kumpe catheter and 0.0.35 glide guide wire, access was gained into the right
subclavian vein and a venogram was obtained, which demonstrated widely patent
central veins with small collateral veins at the level of th eproximal
subclavain vein. Sheath and catheter were removed and a peel- away sheath was
advanced into the SVC under fluoroscopic guidance. The guidewire and inner
portion were removed and a tunneled hemodialysis catheter was placed through
the peel-away sheath with its tip positioned at the right atrium.  A final
chest x- ray demonstrated proper location of the tip at the right atrium.

The neck incision was closed with #4 Vicryl sutures and the catheter was
secured to the skin with 0 Prolene sutures.  The catheter was flushed,
heplocked, and a sterile dressing was applied.  The patient tolerated the
procedure well and there were no immediate complications.  Moderate sedation
was provided by administering divided doses of 50 mcg of fentanyl and 1 mg of
Versed throughout the total intra-service time of 30 minutes during which the
patient's hemodynamic parameters were continuously monitored.

IMPRESSION:  Successful exchange of indwelling temporary hemodialysis catheter
with a 15.5 ___ tunneled hemodialysis catheter with 23 cm tip-to-cuff
length and tip positioned at the right atrium.  The catheter is ready for use.
Patent central veins with small collateral veins at the level of the proximal
right subclavain vein.

INDICATION:  ___ female with subcutaneous areas concerning for
calciphylaxis.  Please evaluate for calcium deposit.

TECHNIQUE:  Axial non-contrast chest CT images are obtained from the hip
joints to the knees.  There are no prior studies for comparison.

FINDINGS:

Evaluation of the visualized portions of the pelvis demonstrates an enlarged
uterus with multiple calcifications most consistent with a large fibroid
uterus.  The uterus is not completely imaged.  There is no significant free
fluid in the visualized portion of the pelvis.  The rectum is distended with a
large amount of stool.

There is moderate degenerative change of both hip joints with joint space
narrowing, osteophyte formation, and subchondral sclerosis.  No fracture is
identified.  There are mild degenerative changes of the pubic symphysis as
well.  Enthesopathy at both ischial tuberosities is noted.

The thighs demonstrate moderate vascular calcification throughout both the
iliac and femoral vessels.  The calcific atherosclerotic change does not
appear exuberant.  No calcified subcutaneous nodules are seen.  No fluid
collection or intramuscular collections are identified in the thighs.  There
is diffuse reticular subcutaneous edema in both thighs.  Prominent venous
varicosities are noted throughout the thighs.  The muscles appear
symmetrically atrophic.

The visualized femurs are normal in appearance.  No lytic or sclerotic lesions
are seen.

The visualized portions of the upper knee joints demonstrate moderate-to-
severe tricompartment osteoarthritic change with osteophyte formation, and
sclerosis.

IMPRESSION:  

1.  Moderate vascular calcific atherosclerosis in the pelvis and both thighs.
No associated soft tissue calcification or subcutaneous nodular calcification
present.

2.  Enlarged uterus with calcified fibroids, incompletely imaged on this exam.

3.  Bilateral osteoarthritic changes of the hips.

INDICATION:  ___ female with skin wound and persistent leukocytosis;
evaluate for underlying osteomyelitis.

TECHNIQUE:  Axial T1 and STIR, coronal T1 and STIR, and sagittal T1 fat
suppressed sequences of the right calf were performed without the use of
gadolinium.  Comparison is made to prior study of ___, however, the
previous exam was extremely limited due to motion artifact.

FINDINGS:

Today's study also demonstrates motion artifact, however, no gross signal
change or edema is present within the visualized muscles of the calf.  No
intramuscular fluid collection is seen.  No fluid tracking along fascial
planes is evident.

Underlying marrow signal is preserved on T1 sequences.  No marrow edema is
present on fluid-sensitive sequences to suggest osteomyelitis.

There is diffuse muscle atrophy.  The subcutaneous tissues are grossly
unremarkable.  Prominent venous varicosities are present.

IMPRESSION:  Limited study demonstrating no signal change to suggest
osteomyelitis.  No muscle abscess or fluid collection present.
